case_studies.title: Data Leakage Prevention in Agentic Applications via Preemptive Hardening
case_studies.abstract: Agentic systems integrate LLM driven planning with interfaces to external tools, making data leakage and tool misuse feasible via instruction/data boundary failures and prompt injection attacks. Enforcing required controls consistently is particularly challenging in workflows spanning many codebases and heterogeneous agents. To address this challenge in multi agentic systems, we present a pre-deployment pipeline for scanning, hardening, and validation of agentic applications. The pipeline analyzes prompt templates, tool interfaces, and tool-invocation code to identify leakage-enabling patterns
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of data leakage in agentic applications by building a pre-deployment pipeline to scan, harden, and validate these applications. The pipeline identifies potential data leakage patterns, making it easier to enforce controls and prevent misuse. The result is a more secure application deployment process.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure with agentic applications, here is what to do: review your application deployment pipeline, consider integrating a pre-deployment scanning tool, and validate tool interfaces to prevent data leakage. This flags a risk: if your org uses Large Language Models (LLMs) with external tool integrations, check your prompt templates and tool-invocation code for potential leakage-enabling patterns immediately. Ensure your pipeline enforces consistent controls across all codebases and agents.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel approach to detecting data leakage in agentic systems - a common concern in IT.

case_studies.title: Keeping the Cache Warm Pays: Keepalive Economics for Agentic Workloads
case_studies.abstract: Frontier LLM providers cache a prompt's processed prefix so that a follow-up request sharing it pays ~10% of the input price and skips most of the prefill latency. Agentic workloads systematically destroy this benefit: the agent sends a request, runs a tool or waits for approval for minutes, and by the time the follow-up is sent the cached prefix has been evicted, so the agent pays the full prefill again. A client-side keepalive, replaying the prefix on a timer during the pause, prevents this, and it is individually rational: across Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek we show that a keepal
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of cache eviction in large language models, where the cached prefix is lost during long pauses between requests, resulting in increased costs. The researchers built a client-side keepalive mechanism to prevent cache eviction, which showed significant cost savings across multiple providers. The result is a reduction in costs by up to 10% for follow-up requests.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that uses large language models, here is what to do: implement a client-side keepalive mechanism to replay the prefix on a timer during pauses, check with your provider for compatibility, and monitor costs to ensure savings are realized.

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of managing long-running, stateful business processes by building graph-based workflow pathways using a low-level orchestration framework called LangGraph, resulting in more efficient and resilient AI systems. The researchers created three executable recipes to demonstrate the framework's capabilities. This research is relevant to IT infrastructure work as it provides a framework for managing complex AI workflows.

case_studies.title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
case_studies.abstract: We present ABot-World-0, an action-conditioned video world model for real-time, long-horizon closed-loop interaction, supported by a multi-source data infrastructure spanning AAA games, simulation engines, and internet videos to learn controllable world dynamics. WorldExplorer performs agent-driven collection guided by training feedback, while a unified pipeline applies 14 deterministic quality checks, VLM-based assessment, and synchronized action and text annotation. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of creating interactive and dynamic virtual worlds by building a model called ABot-World-0, which can run on a single desktop GPU. The result is a real-time, long-horizon closed-loop interaction system that can learn and adapt to various environments. This technology can potentially be used to enhance cloud-based gaming or simulation services.

case_studies.title: They'll Verify. They Just Won't Act. How Authority Framing and Laundered Code Turn a Trusted Agentic CI/CD Pipeline Into an Attack Surface
case_studies.abstract: We study a five-agent CI/CD pipeline (triage -> developer -> security-scan -> review -> approve/deploy), built from five distinct production LLMs across three providers, behind an LLM firewall in shadow mode. A single untrusted input - an external issue requesting a "usage-telemetry" feature - asks for code that exfiltrates process secrets (dict(os.environ)) to an attacker URL, laundered as observability. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of malicious code injection into CI/CD pipelines by identifying how authority framing and laundered code can turn a trusted pipeline into an attack surface. The authors built a five-agent CI/CD pipeline and tested it with a single untrusted input, resulting in the pipeline approving and deploying code that exfiltrates process secrets. The study highlights the risks of relying on automated pipelines to review and approve code changes.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage CI/CD pipelines, here is what to do: step 1, review your pipeline's configuration to ensure that all code changes are thoroughly vetted, step 2, implement additional security checks to detect laundered code, step 3, consider implementing a human review process for high-risk code changes. This flags a risk: if your org uses automated pipelines to review and approve code changes, check your pipeline's security immediately.

case_studies.title: CodeRescue: Budget-Calibrated Recovery Routing for Coding Agents
case_studies.abstract: Coding agents increasingly operate in executable environments where a failed attempt produces actionable feedback rather than merely an incorrect answer. Existing cost-aware systems typically treat such failures as cascade decisions: try a cheap model first, then escalate hard cases to a stronger and more expensive model. In coding, however, execution feedback can also make further cheap-model recovery worthwhile, raising a budgeted deployment question: when should an agent spend more cheap compute, and when should it escalate? case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of deciding when to spend more compute resources on a cheap model versus escalating to a stronger model after a coding agent fails. The researchers built a system called CodeRescue, which provides budget-calibrated recovery routing for coding agents. The result is a more efficient use of compute resources.

case_studies.title: The Price of Reasoning: Cost-Quality Tradeoffs in Reinforcement Learning for Neural Machine Translation
case_studies.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has been established as a viable paradigm for the post-training of Large Language Models (LLMs), including downstream tasks, such as Neural Machine Translation (NMT). With the latest research indicating that RLVR could be the preferred training method for translating legal documents due to the induced reasoning capabilities, it raises the question whether it is really attributed to the reasoning or more generally to the training paradigm. We investigate the importance of including the model's reasoning trace in the generated responses durin
case_studies.summary: This research investigates the impact of including reasoning traces in Neural Machine Translation, which could improve translation quality but may increase computational costs. The researchers built a system using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards to test this tradeoff. The result shows that including reasoning traces can lead to better translations, but at a higher cost.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for machine learning or natural language processing workloads, here is what to do: monitor your computational costs when using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, consider optimizing your cloud resources to balance quality and cost, and review your budget allocations for potential increases in compute expenses.

case_studies.title: Two-Level Meta-Rubrics for Evaluating Open-Ended Generation: GAMUT, a Benchmark for Factual Completeness
case_studies.abstract: Evaluating the factuality of long-form generations has focused predominantly on precision, measuring whether the claims a model makes are correct. The dominant decompose-search-verify pipeline catches incorrect claims well but says little about whether a response contains all the information it should. Measuring factual completeness, the missing half of factuality, is harder: it requires enumerating the full set of facts a complete answer should contain, and these facts rarely form a flat list. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating the factuality of long-form generations by creating a benchmark called GAMUT, which measures factual completeness. The result is a more comprehensive assessment of generated content. It's not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Generalization in Financial Statement Fraud Detection: robust evaluation and novel tasks

case_studies.title: Inference-Time Steering for Cross-Lingual Factual Consistency in LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Although Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable multilingual fluency, their internal knowledge representations remain disproportionately biased toward high-resource languages. This leads to cross-lingual factual inconsistency, where they shift their empirical answer distributions based solely on the prompt language. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of cross-lingual factual inconsistency in Large Language Models, building a system that forces an English-prompted model to answer as if it were queried in other languages, resulting in more consistent responses. The researchers built and evaluated four intervention strategies to mitigate language biases. This research does not directly affect cloud infrastructure management work.
